title: Annotatio V §.II: Against making all dogmas hang on Roman authority — Constance / papal council can inflate the least
pass_a_gloss: who acknowledge no Fundamentals in themselves — whether by immediate Divine authority or by their own nature as founding the Christian faith — but hang all Dogmas of the Christian faith, greatest and least, as to Truth, Necessity, or Fundamentality, upon the Authority of the Roman Church; whereby it comes about that what either touches the Christian faith least, or is adverse to the Christian faith, may nevertheless, this notwithstanding, through some Council of Constance or Papal Council become essential to the Christian faith, even the greatest,
pass_b_english: who own no fundamentals in themselves — neither by immediate divine authority nor by their nature as founding the Christian faith —
but hang every dogma of the faith, great or small, as to truth, necessity, or fundamentality, on the authority of the Roman Church.
So what barely touches the Christian faith, or even runs against it, can still, through some Constance or papal council, become essential to that faith — even the greatest point.
source_text: Fundamentales, sive auctoritate Divinâ eâque immediatâ, sive naturâ suâ talia, quòd fidem Christianam fundant, per se agnoscentes nulla, omnia verò Dogmata fidei Christianae maxima minimaque, tùm quà Veritatem, tùm quà Necessitatem, aut Fundamentalitatem, ab Auctoritate Ecclesiae Romanae suspendentes, quâ fit, ut quod vel fidem Christianam contingit minimum, vel fidei Christianae adversum est, illud nihilominus, hôc non obstante, per Constantiense quoddam, vel Papale Concilium, fidei Christianae essentiale evadat vel maximum,
